status: pre-registered before any graph of the 60 fork-series runs (labels f06, m06) was scored. Known when written: run status (f06 30 of 30 completed; m06 22 of 30, 8 crashes in the cycle step), LLM tokens and cost, and the algorithm chosen; no graph metric.
question: Does refinement v2 inside Causal-Copilot (branch bld-06-refinement-v2) deliver graphs at least as good as the unmodified pipeline on the same 30 BND-08 tables, run on the same image?

runs.history: BND-08 (label s2, analysis/results/stability_s2/bnd08_summary.json), old image: reported beside, not compared by a rule

graphs.S0: results.converted_graph of the run's last state snapshot (the algorithm's output handed to refinement)

reference: datasets/suite_q1s2/MAPPING.json reference_by_data per arm; scores by analysis/cc_graph.score (adjacency F1; directed F1 counting committed directions only)

metrics.delivered_dir_f1: final directed F1, a run that delivered no final graph (crash) scores 0: what a user of the run receives
metrics.both_completed: final adjacency and directed F1 on the arms where both arms' runs completed, paired by arm
metrics.S0: adjacency F1 of S0, all 30 arms paired: the algorithm stage is the same code in both arms, so this checks the two series ran comparable algorithms
metrics.intervals: cluster bootstrap over the 10 scenario families (score/paired.cluster_bootstrap, B = 2000, seed 20261014)

predictions.L1: delivered directed F1: branch minus main >= 0.02 (paired mean over 30 arms)
predictions.L2: both completed: branch final adjacency F1 not below main by more than 0.02 (paired mean)
predictions.L3: S0 adjacency F1: |branch minus main| <= 0.03 (paired mean)

rule.drop_in: L2 holds and L3 holds: refinement v2 removes the crash and cuts cost without losing graph quality on these tables; the Q1 checkpoint (BND-13) shows the changed pipeline as the improved Causal-Copilot
rule.trade_off: L2 fails with L3 holding: v2 costs graph quality; reported as a trade-off; wave C diagnoses with v2's R4-R6 on these runs
rule.incomparable: L3 fails: the two series ran materially different algorithms; quality differences are not attributed to v2

failure_modes_named_in_advance: LLM nondeterminism: one run per arm per series, so per-arm differences include run-to-run noise (BND-08's design); the family bootstrap is the only interval
selection: crashed main runs have no final graph; L2 uses arms where both completed and L1 scores a crash as 0, both stated
S3 (the graph handed to the cycle step) needs the pipeline's pickles and is not used here
